options: Turning off the borrow checker entirely
Mutating a value through a shared `&` reference, with the borrow rules checked at runtime
A way to make all fields public
quiz.explain: Interior mutability lets you change data even when you only hold a shared `&`. The type (like RefCell) enforces the borrow rules itself, at runtime instead of compile time.

quiz.q: What happens if you hold a `RefCell` read borrow and call `borrow_mut()` at the same time?
quiz.explain: RefCell enforces 'many readers or one writer' at runtime. Violating it compiles fine but panics with a BorrowMutError when it runs.

quiz.q: Which combination gives shared ownership AND mutation in single-threaded code?
quiz.explain: `Rc` provides multiple owners and `RefCell` provides interior mutability. Together, several owners can each mutate the shared value (single-threaded).

quiz.q: Why can't you use `RefCell` to share mutable state across threads?
options: It isn't thread-safe (not Sync), so the compiler rejects it; use `Mutex`/`RwLock` instead
quiz.explain: RefCell's runtime borrow tracking isn't thread-safe, so it can't cross thread boundaries. The thread-safe equivalents are Mutex and RwLock.

flashcards.back: Mutate through a shared `&` via `.borrow()` / `.borrow_mut()`, enforcing 'many readers or one writer' at runtime — panicking if you break it.
`Cell` is for small `Copy` values via `get`/`set` and never panics; `RefCell` lends references and checks borrows at runtime.

flashcards.front: The single-thread combo for shared, mutable data?
flashcards.back: `Rc<RefCell<T>>` — Rc for multiple owners, RefCell for interior mutation.
`Arc` replaces `Rc`, and `Mutex`/`RwLock` replace `RefCell`. So `Arc<Mutex<T>>` is the thread-safe twin of `Rc<RefCell<T>>`.
